newsitem.title: INDONESIA: SE Asian Grain - Domestic prices trend easier.
newsitem.headline: SE Asian Grain - Domestic prices trend easier.

text.p: Domestic grain and oilseed prices drifted lower in Southeast Asia this week with stocks comfortable and more imports arriving in markets around the region, traders said on Wednesday.
The harvest in Indonesia, ample stocks in Malaysia and imports in Thailand pressured corn prices, they said.
"Corn has started to trickle in from Lampung (in South Sumatra)," one Lampung trader said. "I think this has begun to put pressure on local prices."
Other traders, however, said harvests in Lampung were expected to start in earnest in late November.
"I don't think the crop coming from Lampung is sizeable at the moment," one Jakarta-based trader said.
He said local corn supply was expected to rise as the government's introduction of hybrid corn was beginning to bear fruit, especially in the key growing region of East Java.
Dealers said corn was quoted at 415-420 rupiah a kg in Jakarta, down from 430-435 rupiah a week ago. Soymeal was around 800-810 rupiah/kg compared with 820 rupiah last week.
One Indonesian trader said domestic soymeal prices were expected to come under pressure from plentiful stocks.
In Malaysia, local grain and oilseed prices were down with buyers staying away for another week because of falling futures prices in Chicago.
A trader at a Kuala Lumpur flour mill said bulk corn for December was being offered at 420 to 430 ringgit a tonne in the central region, compared to spot prices of 475-480 ringgit.
"Today's price is ultimately going to fall 40 to 50 (ringgit) by next month," said the trader.
"A" grade wheat in bags was down to 800 ringgit a tonne ex-factory/godown in the central region, from 840 previously. Low-grade wheat was maintained at between 500 to 510 ringgit.
Local soymeal was lower at 810 ringgit a tonne from 818 previously, while imported soymeal was going for about 800 ringgitt, compared to 810 last week.
Thai soymeal prices slipped as the industry expected more supplies to arrive in the local market later this month.
Corn prices were steady to lower at around 4.25-4.40 baht a kg compared with 4.35-4.38 baht a week ago as rains hampered the transportation of corn to Bangkok, trade sources said.
Otherwise, the market was quiet except for the purchase of 50,000 tonnes of U.S.-origin soybeans by oil crushers last week, they added.
The industry was sidelined awaiting further falls in soymeal prices which would give them an opportunity to buy again as their commercial needs for the year had been largely covered.
"There have been a lot of inquiries, but no buying. The industry might want to wait until prices bottom out," said one trader.

The industry was also waiting for the Commerce Ministry to come up with a concrete policy to protect local farmers after the removal of import quotas on soybeans and soymeal which went into effect from November 1.
The Ministry was seeking a pledge from the industry that it would buy most of the local crop, market sources said.
"There has been some talk about possible import-to-local product ratio. But no conclusion has been reached yet," said one animal feed producer.
Local soymeal prices were quoted easier at around 10.00 baht a kg compared with 10.20 baht a kg last week.
U.S. soymeal was quoted at around US$302-310 C&F Bangkok while Indian-origin soymeal was priced at around $290-295 on the same basis.
"The fact that almost 150,000 tonnes of soymeal and pellets are arriving this month pressured local prices," said one trader.

About 25,193 tonnes of Argentine soymeal were expected to arrive here on November 8 while 53,789 tonnes of soypellet from Brazil was scheduled to arrive on November 10, according to shipping sources. The rest would arrive later this month.
